title: KV background compaction & defrag experiment notes
summary: Working notes on experiments to implement low-latency background compaction (defragmentation) for the KV cache allocator to reduce fragmentation-induced page bloat and optimize memory bandwidth usage.
body:
Background:

We've historically relied on a slab-like allocator + LRU for KV residency and occasional synchronous reclaim when pages are pressured. Over the last two months production traces show growing host memory footprint and degraded page locality for long-sequence workloads (RAG Q&A with long contexts). The hypothesis is that fragmentation (many small freed ranges scattered across hugepage boundaries) causes:

- inflated RSS (lots of partially used pages)
- suboptimal NUMA locality (allocated > freed interleaving across nodes)
- increased DMA churn during spillback/prefetch due to non-contiguous KV segments

Goal: test a low-impact background compaction runnable in the serving runtime that coalesces resident KV ranges into contiguous allocations, reclaiming whole pages and reducing read amplification and DMA overhead while keeping tail latency impact negligible.

Hypotheses to validate:

1) Periodic, rate-limited compaction can reduce RSS by 8–25% on fragmentation-heavy workloads with <1% increase in p99 latency if compaction is staggered per-shard.
2) Aggressive full compaction (stop-the-world) yields more RSS reduction but causes p99 spikes that violate SLOs.
3) NUMA-aware compaction (preferring co-location in same node) shows measurable reduction in host<->GPU DMA cross-node transfers and improves median latency under multi-tenant mixes.

Testbed and baseline:

- Cluster: 8x A100-HBM nodes (4x per node for hosted tests; testbed for allocator experiments is CPU host memory focused) + NVMe for spillback tests.
- Runtime branch: allocator/compaction-experiment (PR linked above).
- Baseline allocator: jemalloc + custom KV slab manager.
- Workloads: 
  - W1: single-tenant long context generation (avg seqlen 2048, hot prefixes)
  - W2: mixed multi-tenant small chat + occasional long RAG (simulated tenant skew 80/20)
  - W3: synthetic churn: allocate/free small KV entries (sizes 512B–64KB) with 30–70% reuse distribution.
- Metrics collected: RSS, resident pages reclaimed, reuse_rate (per-key hits/allocs), p50/p95/p99 latency for forward token, host->GPU DMA MB/s, eviction count, page read amplification (MB read / MB useful).

Instrumentation changes made for these experiments:

- Added compaction tracing spans (compaction.start, compaction.unit, compaction.finish) with coordinator_shard id and bytes_moved.
- Counters for compaction throttled cycles, page_coalesces, contiguous_runs_formed.
- Sampling heap map snapshot per 5s during test to drive heatmaps (script: tools/heapmap.py).

Compaction algorithm (prototype):

- Background worker per shard (cooperative): wakes every 500ms, but has a token bucket allowing X bytes/s movement (configurable).
- Scans allocator free list for small freed runs that are adjacent (within same 2MB hugepage) and attempts an in-place move: allocate contiguous target, memcpy, update KV pointer atomically (lockless CAS with fallback).
- If CAS fails, revert and mark run back; we avoid global stop-the-world.
- NUMA policy: prefer targets on same node if source is hot-read node.
- Staggering: compaction start times are jittered by shard id to avoid synchronized network/DMA spikes.

Workload runs & key results (abridged):

Run A (W1, baseline vs compaction throttled to 50 MB/s per shard):
- baseline RSS: 78.2 GB
- after 30m compaction: 64.9 GB (17% reduction)
- reuse_rate increased marginally (+2.8%) due to better locality
- host->GPU DMA reduced from 410 MB/s avg to 360 MB/s avg (12% reduction)
- p99 latency: baseline 142 ms -> compaction 156 ms (10% increase), but spikes aligned with compaction unit windows; when we reduce throttle to 20 MB/s p99 delta <3%

Run B (W2, multi-tenant, compaction with NUMA policy, 30 MB/s):
- baseline RSS (sum): 120 GB -> after 30m: 104 GB (13% reduction)
- cross-node DMA drops 18% (measured by nvlink/ib counters + host tracer)
- median latency unchanged; p99 improved for the long-tenant (likely fewer cross-node page fetches)

Run C (W3 churn, aggressive compaction at 200 MB/s):
- RSS reduction 28% but severe p99 spikes (250–600 ms) and occasional 1s stalls when large runs moved
- eviction count during compaction windows increased (our allocator triggered extra eviction due to transient double allocations)

Observations / analysis:

- Compaction effectiveness correlates with the density of small freed runs within hugepage regions. Systems with frequent small KV deletes benefit more.
- Throttling is critical. There is a sweet spot ~20–50 MB/s per shard where we reclaim meaningful memory without violating p99 SLOs. Above ~100 MB/s we see amplifying side-effects (eviction churn, allocator contention).
- NUMA sensitivity: when compaction is NUMA-aware we reduce cross-node DMA and improve tail latencies for mixed workloads. The scheduler needs node-local target selection heuristics.
- CAS-based pointer update works 95% of the time in our tests; fallback path increases complexity and latency for the affected keys. Need to bound fallback attempts.
- Interaction with jemalloc arenas: background compaction sometimes contends with the allocator's own background threads. We saw increased stall time when both were active. Consider coordinating with jemalloc tunables or using dedicated arenas for KV cache.

Concrete telemetry to add (next iteration):

- Track per-compaction-unit p99 latency deltas tied to compaction.offset and bytes_moved (so we can correlate a specific compaction job with application latency).
- Heatmap of contiguous_run_length distribution before/after compaction in persistent storage.
- Eviction origin tags: whether eviction triggered during compaction window should be annotated in traces.

Mitigations tried and results:

1) Staggered windows (shard jitter): reduced synchronized spikes; p99 impact shrank by ~40% vs synchronous compaction.
2) Dynamic throttle: reduce compaction rate if p95 latency climbs > 10% in last 30s. This prevented p99 violations but slowed RSS recovery. Good safety valve.
3) Pre-claim targets: pre-allocate target contiguous buffers to avoid allocate-on-move contention. This reduced fallback CAS failures by ~60%. Increases transient memory pressure (requires conservative sizing).

Open questions / risks:

- Long-term behavior under steady-state: will compaction maintain low fragmentation or do freed patterns re-fragment quickly? Need 24–72h runs in cluster to answer.
- Interaction with on-disk spillback and background async reads: moving resident keys may race with inflight spill operations. We must add stronger coordination with spillback subsystem.
- Multi-tenant fairness: Some tenants may lose cache locality during their shard's compaction window — consider tenant-priority exemptions.
- Failure modes for CAS pointer swap: if a pointer is updated mid-move by in-flight request, we have a safe fallback but that had latency implications in tests; quantify probability in prod traces.

Next steps / action items:

- [ ] Run 48h cluster experiment with W2 mix and dynamic throttle enabled (INF-1423 is the ticket). Assigned: Benji. Target: 2025-02-12.
- [ ] Add eviction-origin tagging + heap heatmap export to S3 for postmortem. Assigned: Carlos. Target: 2025-02-07.
- [ ] Prototype jemalloc arena isolation for KV allocator to remove allocator contention. Assigned: Maya. Target: 2025-02-20.
- [ ] Add opt-in per-tenant compaction pause window (tenant-level policy) and test fairness scenarios. Assigned: Aisha. Target: 2025-03-01.

Notes to self / rough ideas:

- Could try a hybrid approach: opportunistic compaction during low-load epochs (night windows per region) and micro-compaction during steady state.
- Explore using madvise/hugepage remap tricks to atomically coalesce ranges without bytewise memcpy (risky but potentially lower CPU move cost).
- Consider integrating with scheduler: compaction should be aware of GPU device memory pressure signals — avoid heavy host compaction when GPUs are starting large jobs.

Log snippets (sample) from compaction span:

[compaction.start shard=7] ts=2025-01-23T03:14:02Z
[compaction.unit shard=7 unit_id=112 bytes_moved=5242880 target_node=0 pages_coalesced=8 cas_success=1 fallback=0 duration_ms=42]
[compaction.finish shard=7 bytes_total=5242880 duration_ms=49]

Conclusion (working): background compaction can meaningfully reduce RSS and cross-node DMA if implemented as a cooperative, rate-limited, NUMA-aware service. The key tradeoffs are throttle tuning, allocator coordination, and safe pointer update semantics. Next experiments should prioritize long-run stability and add richer telemetry to attribute tail-latency events precisely to compaction work.

References / related docs:

- INF-1423 (jira) — feature epic for compaction prototype
- PR 981 — runtime compaction prototype branch
- KV allocator notes on Confluence (link above)

If anyone wants to run the local reproduce: tools/run_compaction_test.sh --workload churn --throttle 30 --duration 1800 --trace compaction-trace.json

Questions for review:

- Are we comfortable shipping a config flag to enable compaction in Dedicated clusters behind a kill-switch? (I think yes with conservative defaults).
- Should we expose per-tenant compaction policies in the console early, or hide behind support? (leaning support-only until we have 48h stability runs)

-- Aisha
